haiku-low.q1: In step 5, after the additive check passes and before any new instance starts, using the new release's migration bundle. The live (old) release must keep working on the migrated schema.
haiku-low.q2: Only in a later release, once the release that still uses the column or table has been retired.
haiku-low.q3: All 4 new instances must pass the health gate (3 consecutive passes each) and the smoke suite within the 10-minute deadline. If not, Abort: listener untouched, new instances stopped, page.
haiku-low.q4: One listener update repoints all traffic from the old target group to the new one at once, conditional on the listener still pointing at old. There is no gradual shift.
haiku-low.q5: A 5xx rate above 1% over a trailing 5-minute window, or metrics unreadable for 3 minutes. Rollback repoints the listener to old, tags groups, stops the failed colour. Migrations are not reversed.
haiku-low.q6: The old colour is held running until T0+30 for a cheap repoint. After that, rollback is a normal deploy of the previous release's SHA, run through the full pipeline.
haiku-low.q7: Migrations already committed stay applied; the failed one rolls back its own transaction. The deploy stops, the new release never starts, the live colour keeps serving, and the owner is paged.
haiku-low.q8: The listener is read fresh each time and is the only authority for the live colour. Release SHA, status and switched_at are kept in tags on each target group.
haiku-low.q9: The pipeline concurrency group catalog-web-deploy lock. A run holds it from step 1 through step 14, about 40 to 50 minutes including the 30-minute hold.
haiku-low.q10: Health checks and smoke tests call the 4 new instances directly at their private addresses, never through the listener, so they get no public traffic before the switch.
haiku-low.q11: The migration tool, run by pipeline step 5 against PostgreSQL. Only unrecorded migrations run, tracked in the tool's own table and guarded by its database lock, assumed to be an advisory lock.
haiku-low.q12: Its instances are deregistered and stopped, and the group is tagged failed or rolled_back. The next deploy's step 3 stops any stray instances, and step 6 overwrites the tags.

sonnet.q1: Step 5, after the additive check (step 4) passes and before any new-release instance starts. The old (live) release must keep working on the migrated schema.
sonnet.q2: Only in a later release, once the release that still uses the column/table has been retired.
sonnet.q3: All 4 new instances must pass the health gate (3 consecutive passes each) and the full smoke suite, within the shared 10-minute deadline from the start request. If not, Abort: listener untouched, new instances deregistered and stopped, new group tagged failed, run fails and pages (listing applied migrations; database ahead of live release).
sonnet.q4: In one step (no gradual shift): a single conditional listener update repoints the public listener from the old target group to the new one (step 10).
sonnet.q5: A breach (trailing 5-minute 5xx rate above 1% at any minute check from T0+5 to T0+15), or metrics unreadable for 3 consecutive minutes. It repoints the listener back to the old group, tags old live and new rolled_back, then stops the failed colour's 4 instances, fails the run, skips steps 12 and 13, and pages. It leaves the old colour untouched (nothing to start) and never reverses migrations.
sonnet.q6: 30 minutes after the switch (T0 to T0+30), while the old colour stays running; an engineer's rollback job can repoint. After the old colour is shut down, a problem is handled by a normal deploy of the previous release's SHA (the release tag on the retired group), skipping the build; migrations stay applied.
sonnet.q7: The failed migration rolls back its own transaction; earlier migrations that already committed stay applied (additive, so the live release is unaffected). The deploy stops, the new release is never started, the live colour keeps serving, and the owner is paged naming the failed migration. The next deploy only sees the unrecorded migrations.
sonnet.q8: Read fresh from the listener each time, which is the only authority. The new colour is simply the opposite of the listener. Recorded in the listener itself; the live group's tags (status, release SHA, switched_at) must agree with it, but are not the authority.
sonnet.q9: The pipeline concurrency group lock catalog-web-deploy. It is held from step 1 to step 14, about 40 to 50 minutes, including the full 30-minute hold.
sonnet.q10: The pipeline job calls the 4 new instances directly on their private addresses, never through the listener (the pipeline runner is assumed to reach them).
sonnet.q11: The pipeline job in step 5 runs the new release's migration bundle, one transaction per migration, under the migration tool's database lock (assumed to be a PostgreSQL advisory lock). Only migrations not recorded as applied in the tool's table run, and a deploy runs the step once.
sonnet.q12: They are deregistered and stopped (abort: new group tagged failed; rollback 11a: new group tagged rolled_back, instances stopped after the repoint is confirmed). The tag is kept until the next deploy's step 6 overwrites it. The next deploy ignores idle-colour tags, and step 3 stops any stray instances and requires 0 running there.
